title: Resting-state EEG data before and after cognitive activity across the adult lifespan and a 5-year follow-up
description: This dataset contains 64-channel resting-state EEG from 608 healthy adults aged 20-70 years, recorded for three minutes each with eyes closed and eyes open. Recordings were made before and after a 2-hour block of demanding cognitive tasks. A subsample of 208 participants also completed a follow-up session about five years after baseline. The data come from the Dortmund Vital Study on healthy cognitive aging and are provided as raw, non-preprocessed EEG in BIDS format.
methods_description: Resting-state EEG was recorded in a quiet laboratory with participants seated, using a 64-channel actiCap system (10-20 layout, FCz online reference) and a BrainVision BrainAmp DC amplifier. Sampling rate was 1000 Hz with a 250 Hz online low-pass filter, and impedances were kept below 10 kOhm. Eyes-closed recording always preceded eyes-open recording, and both were done before and after a 2-hour cognitive task block.

funding_references.funder_name: The Dortmund Vital Study is funded by the institute’s budget (no grant number). Thus, the study design, collection, management, analysis, interpretation of data, writing of the report, and the decision to submit the report for publication is not influenced or biased by any sponsor.
